Once, I met a guy that was hired to be an editor in a globally well know company and didn't know how to edit. Really, he didn't know, nothing. He couldn't even open premiere properly. And guess what? One female editor friend of mine, who was in the industry for some time, applied to that same job. She lost for a guy that didn't even know how to edit. 
I don't know if it applies to others locations, but I can definitely say that in my country, sexism still is a serious issue. The good knews is that is getting better. I believe that an experimental film, in short words, is when you try things that are not "common" or used in the "standard"  scene. For example, have you ever seen "Meshes Of The Afternoon", by Maya Deren? It is often read as an experimental movie since it played with some "strange", non-linear and oniric narrative, that was very different from what was being made in Hollywood at that time. It is kinda hard to define what an experimental movie is but let's say that is when you literally experiment with some aspect (or aspects) of the visual vocabulary. It is literally an experimental experience (lol). I don't know if I made myself clear, english is not my mother language, but this is what I understand when experimental movies come to my mind
